name: com.aeralas.maps/aerial-maps
title: Aeralas Maps
description: Print-ready annotated aerial maps of US addresses. Free previews; pay by card link or x402.

tools.name: get_service_info
tools.description: What the maps contain, the price, imagery coverage and quality, how to pay over x402, and how a person can buy one directly. Free.

tools.name: check_coverage
tools.description: Address or point in; imagery source and how sharp it prints, parcel availability and overlays out. Outside coverage it says so and what would work instead. One cheap call: use it before anything else when the place might not be covered. Continental US, plus Hawaii and Alaska on regional frames. Free.

address.description: A US street address, a city and state, or a ZIP code.

center.description: [longitude, latitude] in WGS84. Alternative to address.

groundWidthM.description: The frame you have in mind: how wide, in metres of ground.

tools.name: check_map
tools.description: Lay out the map and report what it had to compromise on -- overlapping labels, truncated text, annotations off the page -- each with the annotation, a code and the fix as data; plus the imagery quality, everything drawn (with its place on the ground and box on the page) and what was dropped. Returns no image. Free; iterate here before buying.

address.description: Continental US only, plus Hawaii and Alaska on regional frames (groundWidthM 3300 or more). Where to centre the map: a US street address with city and state ("1750 Elm St, Manchester, NH"), or just a city and state ("Tualatin, OR") or a ZIP code for a map of the area.

center.description: [longitude, latitude] in WGS84. Alternative to address. Continental US only, plus Hawaii and Alaska on regional frames (groundWidthM 3300 or more).

groundWidthM.description: True ground width of the frame in meters. 500 fits a typical retail plaza; 20000-40000 makes a regional map, where autoLabel drafts cities, highway shields and water instead of tenants.

imagerySourceId.description: Imagery source id. Defaults to the sharpest source covering the frame.

annotations.description: Callouts to draw. Placement, collision avoidance and leader lines are automatic.

id.description: Your id for this annotation. Echoed back in warnings so you can match them up.

at.description: [lon, lat]. Required for tenant_callout and traffic_count.

path.description: [[lon,lat],...] along the road. Required for road_label.

network.description: route_shield: interstate, US route or state route.

monogram.description: subject_pin: up to three characters shown in the pin, e.g. initials.

stat.description: panel: the figure in the header, e.g. "100,000+ jobs".

body.description: panel: a grid of logos, one large logo, a photo, or header only.

name.description: Brand name, looked up for a public-domain logo.

image.description: Your own logo as a data: URI (PNG, JPEG or WebP).

photo.description: panel: a photo as a data: URI (PNG, JPEG or WebP), up to 8 MB.

outline.description: panel: the offset frame. Default on.

width.description: panel: width as a fraction of the page.

anchor.description: panel: top-left corner as fractions of the page. Omit to dock the panel beside the place it points at.

stylePreset.description: light reads on dark pavement and roofs in shadow; dark reads on bright roofs and sunlit parking; accent is survey orange, meant for the subject property only.

offset.description: Move the label box relative to its pin, in preview pixels (the page is 1397 wide at 11x17 portrait). Setting this turns the auto-placer OFF for this annotation, so it is the fix for a label_overlap warning you want resolved a specific way.

textScale.description: Multiplier on text size. Lower it to clear a text_truncated warning.

strokeScale.description: Multiplier on pin, leader and outline weights.

boxColor.description: CSS colour for the label box fill.

inkColor.description: CSS colour for the label text.

markColor.description: CSS colour for the pin and leader line.

autoLabel.description: Draft tenant callouts from open business data (Overture Maps) and road names from Census TIGER before drawing your own. Use this when you do not know what is at the location. Pass an object to control how many: fewer labels is the simplest cure for a crowded page.

mode.description: site drafts tenants and road names; regional drafts cities, highway shields and water. auto picks regional for frames 3000 m wide or more.

brandsOnly.description: Keep only recognised chains. A flyer wants anchors, not every barber.

labelScale.description: Text size multiplier applied to every annotation that does not set its own textScale. Drop to ~0.8 to fit more labels; raise for a map read at arm’s length.

titleBlockScale.description: Size multiplier for the title block.

overlays.description: Thematic layers drawn under the annotations. A legend is added automatically. fema-flood: regulated floodplain (blank means no mapped hazard — FEMA draws Zone X with no symbol). nwi-wetlands: USFWS National Wetlands Inventory. parcels: tax parcel lines for every lot in the frame, on site maps up to 3 km wide, in the states listed under parcels in the docs.

subjectParcel.description: Outline the property itself: finds its tax parcel and draws it as the subject property. With an address, the parcel is the one recorded at that street address; with center or subjectParcel.at, the one under that point. Available in the states listed under parcels in the docs. The check response says which parcel was picked (number, address, acres) so you can confirm it before buying. If none is found the map is still drawn, with a parcel_not_found warning.

at.description: [longitude, latitude] of a point on the property. Use when there is no street address, or when the state records none for its parcels.

label.description: Text for the outline, e.g. "SITE" or "2.3 AC".

recenter.description: On a map located by address, centre the frame on the parcel instead of on the geocoded point, which sits on the road and can be a lot or two away. Has no effect when you give center: that frame is yours.

pageElements.description: Page furniture. Turn elements off to free up room for labels.

locatorInset.description: A small USGS topo overview showing where this frame sits in the wider area, with the frame outlined on it. Worth the corner it costs whenever the reader may not know the town.

insetZoomOut.description: How many times wider than the frame the inset covers.

title.description: Title block heading. Defaults to the address.

mapId.description: Revise a map you already bought. Returned as X-Map-Id on your paid export. Re-exports are free for 7 days as long as the FRAME is unchanged — change labels, styling, overlays and page elements freely; changing address, center, groundWidthM, pageSize, orientation or dpi makes it a different map.

tools.name: preview_map
tools.description: Render the map at screen size with a PREVIEW watermark: the image, a link to it good for 7 days, everything drawn and dropped, warnings with fixes, and payUrl -- the page to give your user, where they see the map and pay $39 by card. Same request as make_map. Free.

tools.name: make_map
tools.description: Buy the print-resolution map. No wallet? Call it once: it returns a link to give your user, who pays $39 by card with no account, and an order id for check_order (preview_map returns the same link). With an x402 wallet it renders the map and returns a download link, priced by what the request asks for, in USDC: Backdrop $0.50, Labelled map $0.75, Site map $1.00 (get_service_info has the rule). The first call returns the payment requirements with the exact amount; sign and call again with the payment. Charged only if the render succeeds. Includes 7 days of free revisions via revise_map. With the mapId of a map already bought, adds what a dearer tier includes for the difference. Overlays and panel annotations are sold only by card ($39, which also opens the map in the editor): asked for here, make_map returns a card payment link instead.

tools.name: check_order
tools.description: When make_map could not be paid over x402, it returns a card payment link for the user and an order id. Call this with that order id after the user says they have paid: it returns the download link and a mapId for free revisions, or says the order is still awaiting payment.

tools.name: revise_map
tools.description: Re-export a map bought with make_map, free for 7 days: change labels, annotations, styling or page elements within the tier you bought. The frame must stay the same -- address or center, groundWidthM, pageSize, orientation, dpi. Requires the mapId make_map returned.
